turns.user_utterance: Using an ATM caused me to incur an additional fee. Why?
turns.assistant_response: Sorry about that—additional fees from an ATM can happen for a few reasons (for example, the ATM operator’s own charge or a foreign-currency/withdrawal fee). Was the withdrawal made in a different currency than your card’s base currency?

turns.user_utterance: No, it was in the same currency as my card.
turns.assistant_response: Thanks—if it was the same currency, the fee is usually either an ATM operator charge or your card’s cash-withdrawal fee/markup. Which country (and whether the ATM is abroad) did you withdraw from, and do you see the fee on your statement as an ATM fee or a cash withdrawal fee?

turns.user_utterance: I withdrew in the UK and the statement just shows it as an “ATM fee.”
turns.assistant_response: In the UK, it’s common for the ATM operator to charge a separate fee—so your statement shows it as an “ATM fee.” This is distinct from any exchange-rate charges (since you withdrew in the same currency). If you share the approximate fee amount and whether you withdrew from a standalone ATM vs a bank (e.g., at a branch), I can help pinpoint what portion is operator vs card/cash-withdrawal fees.
